question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹80, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for Principal when 2-year Simple Interest (SI) and Compound Interest (CI) are given:

P = (SI)² ÷ [4 × (CI − SI)]

⇒ P = (40)² ÷ [4 × (80 − 40)]

⇒ P = 1600 ÷ [4 × 40]

⇒ P = 1600 ÷ 160 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Principal P

 
 1st Yr SI: ₹20

 
 2nd Yr SI: ₹20

 
 Interest: ₹40

 Total CI = 20 + 20 + 40 = ₹80

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹40

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹80

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

⇒ In Compound Interest, additional interest is earned on the 1st year's interest during the 2nd year.

⇒ Total Compound Interest = 1st year SI + 2nd year SI + Interest on 1st year SI

⇒ 80 = 20 + 20 + Interest on 1st year SI

⇒ Interest on 1st year SI = 80 − 40 = ₹40

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest on 1st year SI ÷ 1st year SI) × 100

⇒ R = (40 ÷ 20) × 100 = 200%

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = (Principal × R × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = (P × 200) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = 2P

⇒ P = 10

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for two years is directly calculated as D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Difference between CI and SI for 3 Years

For a period of three years, the formula extends to D = P × (R ÷ 100)² × [(300 + R) ÷ 100].

Ratio of CI and SI for 2 Years

The relationship between Compound Interest and Simple Interest over exactly two years can be expressed as CI ÷ SI = (200 + R) ÷ 200.
